newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.6 from 10.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.6 from 10.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 11.6 percent on Monday from 10.1 percent after bank lenders raised their prices due to poor liquidity.
The day's money market trade fetched 58.2 million kuna, leaving five million kuna worth of unmet demand. Two thirds of the total were rolled over loans.
Call money rose again to 9.0 from 8.0 percent in new trade and the one-week interbank rate rose to 11 from 10.5 percent.
One-day and call money deals were renewed by banks at an unchanged 8.0 percent, and one-week deals at 10.5 percent.
The 30-day rates ranged between 12 and 18 percent, with savings banks paying higher prices. They lent 15-day funds at 13.5 percent.
The central bank said it was mulling a purchase of hard currency from banks but had no date yet for an intervention.
Its kuna midrates for Tuesday firmed to 6.2222 versus 6.2484 against the dollar and to 3.5689 versus 3.5699 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
